subChunks.title: Array Basics

storyBeats.text: Archmage Eldrin leads you to a long stone shelf in the Arcane Library. Exactly five identically shaped vials stand in a row, each numbered from 0 to 4.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: This shelf is an array. Every slot holds the same type of essence, and each slot has a number — its index. The first slot is always zero, never one. Many apprentices stumble on that.

storyBeats.label: Shelf of potions
storyBeats.code:
int[] potions = {100, 75, 50, 25, 10};
System.out.println(potions[0]); // 100  — first
System.out.println(potions[4]); // 10   — last
System.out.println(potions.length); // 5

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: The shelf's length is fixed. You cannot magically conjure a sixth slot. If you reach for slot five, the spell backfires — an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Always check your bounds.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Declare an array int[] scores with five values: 85, 92, 78, 96, 88. Print each element on its own line.
guidedPractice.hint: Use an index-based for loop from 0 to scores.length - 1 and print scores[i] each iteration.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain what an array is in Java, how you declare one, and what happens if you access an invalid index.

questions.prompt: What is the index of the first element in a Java array?
questions.explanation: Java arrays are zero-indexed — the first element is always at index 0.

questions.prompt: You can change the size of a Java array after it has been created.
questions.explanation: Java arrays have a fixed size. Once created, their length cannot change. If you need a resizable container, use ArrayList.
arr[1] is 20 and arr[3] is 40. Their sum is 60.

subChunks.title: Array Operations & Algorithms

storyBeats.text: Eldrin tips five differently-powered vials onto the workbench and slides a quill towards you.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Every master of the arcane arts learns three fundamental operations: traverse every element, find the strongest, and sum the total power. These are the building blocks of every array algorithm you will ever write.

storyBeats.label: Sum and maximum

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: And when you need them sorted, spare yourself the drudgery — the Arrays grimoire has already written that spell for you.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Given int[] vals = {42, 7, 88, 13, 55}, print the sum of all elements on one line, then the largest value on the next line.
guidedPractice.hint: Initialise max = vals[0], then loop through the array updating both sum and max.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain how to find the maximum value in an array without using built-in sort. Walk through the algorithm step by step.

questions.explanation: Arrays.sort() sorts in ascending order in place. Arrays.toString() formats the result.

questions.prompt: You need to find a value in an array without using any library methods. Which approach is correct?
options: Loop through every element and compare
questions.answer: Loop through every element and compare
questions.explanation: Linear search loops through each element comparing it to the target. Arrays don't have find() or indexOf() methods — those belong to ArrayList.

questions.prompt: Arrays.sort() returns a new sorted array and leaves the original unchanged.
questions.explanation: Arrays.sort() sorts the array in place. The original array is modified. Use Arrays.copyOf() first if you need to preserve the original.

subChunks.title: Multi-dimensional Arrays

storyBeats.text: Eldrin unrolls a map of the Academy's potion storage vault — a vast grid of rows and columns, each cell holding a different ingredient.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: One dimension is a shelf. Two dimensions are a room of shelves. You address any cell with two coordinates — row first, then column. Always row, then column.

storyBeats.label: Identity matrix

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Nested loops are the incantation for 2D arrays. The outer loop walks the rows; the inner loop walks each cell within the row. Never confuse the two.

guidedPractice.problemHtml:
Create a 3×3 multiplication table: grid[i][j] = (i+1) * (j+1). Print each row with values separated by spaces.

Expected output:

1 2 3 
2 4 6 
3 6 9
guidedPractice.hint: Use two nested for loops. Outer loop over rows (i), inner loop over columns (j). Print grid[i][j] + " " then println() after each row.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: How do you declare, initialise, and iterate over a 2D array in Java? Give an example of a real-world problem it would model well.

questions.prompt: Given int[][] m = new int[4][6], how many elements does it contain?

questions.explanation: m.length is the number of rows (3). m[0].length is the number of columns in row 0 (2).

questions.prompt: All rows in a Java 2D array must have the same length.
questions.explanation: Java supports jagged arrays — each row is an independent array and can have a different length. However, rectangular 2D arrays (all rows same length) are far more common.
